cards.text: Grab your apron, friend. Chronicles is walking through Israel's families tribe by tribe, and today we pick up the tribes still left, starting with Issachar. Issachar has four sons, and Tola's sons become heads of their families.

cards.question: Tola's descendants are counted in their genealogies as 22,600 mighty men of valor. When does that count happen?
On top of their five chiefs, Izrahiah's family in Issachar has 36,000 troops for battle. True or false: the reason given is that they hired soldiers from other lands.

cards.text: Issachar's mighty men total 87,000. Then Benjamin's families roll by, then Naphtali, who gets one verse. ONE. Friend, I can't say good morning in one verse. Then Manasseh, where a man named Zelophehad has only daughters.

Next up is Ephraim, Joseph's son (Genesis 41:52). Then the list stops cold: Ezer and Elead are killed by the men of Gath, a Philistine city (1 Samuel 6:17), and the text says it happened because they went down to steal livestock.

cards.question: Ezer and Elead were Ephraim's sons. True or false: after their death, Ephraim mourns for many days, and his relatives come to comfort him.
Later, Ephraim's wife gives birth to another son. Ephraim names him Beriah, because ___ had come upon his house.
Sheerah, a daughter in Ephraim's family, gets a line all her own. True or false: she builds towns, including Lower and Upper Beth-horon.
Ephraim's family line runs on, son after son, all the way down to a man named Nun. Who is Nun's son?

cards.text: Finding JOSHUA, the man who led Israel into the land after Moses (Joshua 1:1-2), in this list is like digging through a junk drawer and finding the good scissors. Joseph's descendants settle towns like Bethel, Shechem, Gezer and Megiddo.

Then comes Asher: sons, a couple of sisters, and family after family, called choice and mighty men of valor, with 26,000 fit for battle. Choice and mighty! The nicest thing anybody ever wrote on me was a price sticker that said 25 cents.
Then the list circles back to Benjamin for a closer look. Some families living in Geba are carried into exile, one man has sons in Moab, and a man named Shemed builds the towns of Ono and Lod.

cards.question: In Benjamin's line, Elpaal's sons Beriah and Shema head families living in ___, and they drive out the people of ___.

cards.text: Then come the sons of Beriah, Elpaal, Shimei, Shashak and Jeroham, name after name. And that's a different Beriah than Ephraim's son, like two guys named Mike in the same group chat.

cards.question: All these Benjamite heads of families, the chiefs in their genealogies, live in ___.

cards.text: Then there's Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, who lives in Gibeon with his wife Maacah and a long line of sons. And then the list lands on a name you'll know.

cards.question: In Benjamin's line, Ner was the father of Kish. Who was Kish's son?
Four of Saul's sons are listed here. True or false: one of them is Jonathan.

cards.text: Saul became Israel's king (1 Samuel 11:15), and the sons listed here are Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab and Esh-baal. Jonathan's line runs on through Merib-baal and Micah, all the way down to Azel and his brother Eshek.

cards.question: Eshek's firstborn, Ulam, has sons who are mighty men of valor, with 150 sons and grandsons in all. What kind of fighters are Ulam's sons?

findings.problem: The stop repeatedly quizzes genealogies and name lists: cards 2, 3, 6-9, 13, 15, 17, 18 and 20 all ask about details inside those stretches. The embedded Ephraim family anecdotes do not permit choice cards either; the rule explicitly treats a short story inside a genealogy as part of the stretch.

rule.text: Papa Dorin sums up the stretch in one story card. A short story inside the stretch, like Nimrod in the list of nations (Genesis 10:8–12), is part of the stretch: it can be the standout detail on that card, but it gets no choice cards. A stretch never gets a stop of its own. Its one card sits in the stop with the moments around it. He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item. He can name a standout detail the text gives if it helps the stretch stick. The baker should know the stretch is there and what it's about, not memorize it. A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: Most of the choice cards require luck or outside recall rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. There is no contextual basis for picking the answers on cards 2, 3, 8, 9, 13, 15, 17, 18 or 20. Only cards 6 and 7 provide meaningful reasoning context, so discovery questions dominate the stop instead of remaining a few exceptions.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
